Sanjaya Kumar Mishra vs Smt. Kabita Mishra on 12 January,
2024
Bench: Arindam Sinha, M.S. Sahoo

In The High Court Of Orissa At Cuttack
 Mata No. 265 of 2022
 Sanjaya Kumar Mishra .... Appellant

entities.text: High Court Of Orissa At Cuttack
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Mr. Debaraj Mohanty, Advocate
 -versus-
 Smt. Kabita Mishra .... Respondent

Mr. Gopinath Mishra, Advocate
 Coram:
 Justice Arindam Sinha
 Justice M.S. Sahoo
 Order
12.01.2024 W.P.(C) no.265 of 2022 and I.A. no.452 of 2023 Order No.

Mr. Mohanty, learned advocate appears on behalf of appellant- husband and submits, his client is aggrieved by judgment dated 31 st October, 2022 of the family Court in respect of the permanent alimony directed at 12,00,000/-.
Drawing attention to the judgment he demonstrates that 25% of his client's salary was taken as multiplied by 14 multiplier to arrive at a figure rounded off at 12,00,000/-.

The multiplier was taken from view of a Division Bench of this Court in // 2 // MATA no.44 of 2015 by judgment dated 18th December, 2018 (Bandita Mishra v. Ramakrishna Mishra).
2.
Mr. Mishra, learned advocate appears on behalf of respondent- wife and submits, the multiplier was taken at a figure less than what is provided in the second schedule to Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
3. The second schedule provides multipliers to calculate compensation for third parties in fatal accidents/injury cases claim.
The parameters for the calculation in the schedule are based on what the person, who was/is a victim in the road accident was earning, to compensate for loss of the same by reason of death or injury.

That concept whether can be directly applied for calculating permanent alimony is to be examined because the spouse in the marriage dissolved directed to pay and the other to receive the permanent alimony does not involve loss of earning by the spouse to be Sanjaya Kumar Mishra vs Smt. Kabita Mishra on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7304782/
1 compensated.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the contrary, Court has to keep in mind that the spouse in a dissolved marriage requires permanent alimony without losing sight of the fact that the paying spouse also has a life to lead.
4. Mr. Mohanty prays for stay of execution.
The direction for permanent alimony being akin to a money decree, appellant must put in cash security of 5,00,000/- with Registrar (Judicial) of this Court.
There will be unconditional stay of execution till 12th February, 2024.
In event the security is put in, Registrar (Judicial) shall invest the same in short term deposit yielding maximum rate of interest given by any nationalized bank.
The deposit is to be kept renewed and held in favour of the litigation.
In that event the stay will continue.
Otherwise, on omission to make the deposit the unconditional stay will stand automatically vacated as on and from 13th February, 2024.
6. Mr. Mishra submits, his client has filed a cross-objection for enhancement.
7. List on 19th February, 2024.

(Arindam Sinha) Judge (M.S. Sahoo) Judge Sks Designation: PERSONAL ASSISTANT Sanjaya Kumar Mishra vs Smt. Kabita Mishra on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7304782/
